tradingPermission.method: debug_traceTransaction (callTracer) of mainnet router txs: every router entry point calls Authorization.verifyWitnessSignature with permission argument 2
tradingPermission.whyItCannotMoveFunds: Every router action traced (place / cancel / cancel-all and their operator wrappers) checks permission 2 and only reaches OrdersManager / PerpsManager / FeeManager plus one CollateralManager margin-accounting call (0xdf3e62dd) inside order settlement. Withdrawals are CollateralManager.withdraw called directly by the ACCOUNT (msg.sender, tx 0x74d5cc53ae8de64ce2f9c60da2e110f50faad3f428d09757f9bed3fcc3e8ee41), deposits CollateralManager.deposit(address,address,uint256) — neither goes through a signer permit. perp-cli additionally disables 0, 3 and 4 (permission 1 is the all-bits mask; disabling it wipes trading too, testnet 2026-10-28). Residual: without verified source a future permission-2 router action that moves funds cannot be ruled out; verify (perp wallet agent verify risex) re-reads the on-chain state.

sessionKeysBitmap.layout: sessionKeys(address account, address signer) (0x96ade1f9) returns three 32-byte words: [0] expiration (uint32 unix s, equals RegisterSigner.expiration), [1] permission bitmap, [2] status (1 Active, 3 Revoked, 0 none)

idsAbove4.disablePermission(acct, unregistered sig: revert 0x3b94fe24 SignerNotAuthorized(address) — the id is accepted, the signature check fails
idsAbove4.other setters: none in the bytecode selector list: registerSigner / registerSenderSigner take no permission argument; enablePermission / disablePermission take the same uint8 enum

sessionKeysBitmap.conclusion: Bits 5–31 of a new signer's bitmap cannot be cleared by any function of the reviewed implementation and map to no permission id (ids ≥5 are rejected at ABI decoding). Requiring the raw bitmap to equal exactly 1<<2 would reject every signer. perp-cli instead requires bits 0..4 == 0b00100 on the raw bitmap, status 1, the pinned implementation, and that permission id 5 does not exist — refusing trading the moment the contract is upgraded or gains an id ≥5. Unverified (no gas on testnet): that disablePermission(p) clears exactly bit p; the check fails closed (approve fails → auto-revoke) if it does not.
sessionKeysBitmap.residual: All three contracts are upgradeable proxies controlled by RISEx admin keys; a RISEx-side upgrade can change what a registered signer may do. perp-cli cannot prevent that: it pins each implementation (and the registry address) and refuses every signed action, including cancels, the moment any of them changes (re-checked at least every 60 s in long-lived processes). The window between an upgrade and the next check is not covered.
